```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(knitr)
library(ggplot2)

# Assumptions: every number in this report is derived from these values ------
alpha_main <- 0.05   # significance level
f2_main    <- 0.02   # target effect size (Cohen's small)
N_target   <- 400    # valid responses (Programme Proposal)
N_min      <- 250    # stated minimum (Programme Proposal)
P          <- 12     # predictors in the adjusted model: 3 focal + ~9 covariate terms
P_sub      <- 8      # predictors in subgroup models (RQ3)
miss       <- 0.15   # cases lost to item non-response (complete-case analysis)
excl       <- 0.15   # completed surveys excluded at data-quality screening
rel_x      <- 0.80   # reliability of study-developed climate items
rel_y      <- 0.90   # reliability of K10
consent    <- 0.70   # optional consent to locality linkage (RQ4)
n_sub      <- 100    # expected RQ3 subgroup size (plan: 80-120)
rho_main   <- 0.30   # correlation among the three stressors
f2_int     <- 0.01   # typical interaction effect
optin      <- 0.60   # recontact opt-in (Project Plan target)
resp       <- 0.70   # response per wave among those recontacted
reps       <- 2000   # simulated datasets per scenario

# Analytic power: noncentral F with lambda = f2 * N (G*Power, fixed predictors) --
power_f2 <- function(f2, n, u = 1, p = P, alpha = alpha_main) {
  v    <- n - p - 1
  crit <- qf(1 - alpha, u, v)
  pf(crit, u, v, ncp = f2 * n, lower.tail = FALSE)
}

n_for_power <- function(f2, target = 0.80, ...) {
  n <- 20
  while (power_f2(f2, n, ...) < target) n <- n + 1
  n
}

f2_detectable <- function(n, target = 0.80, ...) {
  uniroot(function(f2) power_f2(f2, n, ...) - target, c(1e-4, 2))$root
}

f2_to_r  <- function(f2) sqrt(f2 / (1 + f2))                 # partial r, one predictor
r_to_f2  <- function(r) r^2 / (1 - r^2)
r2_j     <- function(rho) { S <- matrix(rho, 3, 3); diag(S) <- 1; 1 - 1 / solve(S)[1, 1] }
restrict <- function(r, k) r * k / sqrt(1 - r^2 + r^2 * k^2)  # Thorndike Case II, k = SD ratio
pct      <- function(x) sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * x)
# Keep headers and captions in sync with the assumptions
fixn <- function(x) {
  x <- gsub("N = 400", paste("N =", N_target), x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("N = 340", paste("N =", N_cc), x, fixed = TRUE)
  gsub("400 valid", paste(N_target, "valid"), x, fixed = TRUE)
}
ktab <- function(df, ...) { names(df) <- fixn(names(df)); kable(df, ...) }

# Derived quantities -----------------------------------------------------------
N_cc    <- round(N_target * (1 - miss))         # analysed after missing data
N_gross <- ceiling(N_target / (1 - excl))       # completed surveys for N_target valid
N_link  <- floor(N_target * consent)            # RQ4 analysed sample
f2_att  <- r_to_f2(f2_to_r(f2_main) * sqrt(rel_x * rel_y))   # attenuated effect
a_lab   <- sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.2f", alpha_main))       # alpha label, e.g. ".05"
```

```{r}
#| label: simulation
#| include: false
# X1 = focal stressor; X2, X3 = correlated stressors; Z = covariates.
# beta is set so the population partial f2 for X1 equals f2.
sim_power <- function(n = N_target, f2 = f2_main, rho = rho_main, k_cov = P - 3,
                      errors = c("normal", "skewed"), cut = NULL, careless = 0) {
  errors <- match.arg(errors)
  S <- matrix(rho, 3, 3); diag(S) <- 1
  L <- chol(S)
  beta <- sqrt(f2 / (1 - r2_j(rho)))
  hits <- logical(reps)
  for (r in seq_len(reps)) {
    X <- matrix(rnorm(n * 3), n) %*% L
    Z <- matrix(rnorm(n * k_cov), n)
    e <- if (errors == "normal") rnorm(n) else {
      v <- rlnorm(n, 0, 0.8)                                  # right-skewed, like K10
      (v - exp(0.32)) / sqrt((exp(0.64) - 1) * exp(0.64))    # mean 0, variance 1
    }
    y <- beta * X[, 1] + 0.1 * X[, 2] + 0.1 * X[, 3] + Z %*% rep(0.1, k_cov) + e
    if (careless > 0) {
      # Random responders answer each item independently, so their stressor
      # scores are uncorrelated with each other and with their outcome.
      idx <- sample(n, round(careless * n))
      X[idx, ] <- matrix(rnorm(length(idx) * 3), length(idx))
      y[idx] <- sample(y, length(idx))
    }
    d <- data.frame(y = as.numeric(y), X, Z)
    p <- if (is.null(cut)) {
      summary(lm(y ~ ., d))$coefficients["X1", 4]
    } else {                                                  # outcome dichotomised
      d$y <- as.integer(d$y > quantile(d$y, 1 - cut))
      summary(glm(y ~ ., binomial, d))$coefficients["X1", 4]
    }
    hits[r] <- p < alpha_main
  }
  mean(hits)
}

set.seed(2027)
sim <- c(
  null     = sim_power(f2 = 0),
  baseline = sim_power(),
  skewed   = sim_power(errors = "skewed"),
  median   = sim_power(cut = 0.5),
  top20    = sim_power(cut = 0.2),
  care10   = sim_power(careless = 0.1),
  care20   = sim_power(careless = 0.2)
)

# Two looks at the data (halfway and at the end), each at alpha = .05
z1 <- rnorm(1e6); z2 <- sqrt(0.5) * z1 + sqrt(0.5) * rnorm(1e6)
two_looks <- mean(abs(z1) > qnorm(1 - alpha_main / 2) | abs(z2) > qnorm(1 - alpha_main / 2))
```

```{r}
#| label: key-numbers
#| include: false
p_claim <- power_f2(f2_main, N_target)
p_block <- power_f2(f2_main, N_target, u = 3)
n_block <- n_for_power(f2_main, u = 3)
p_real  <- power_f2(f2_att, N_cc)
p_min   <- power_f2(f2_main, N_min)
p_strict <- pf(qf(1 - alpha_main, 1, N_target - P - 1), 1, N_target - P - 1,
               ncp = f2_main * (N_target - P - 1), lower.tail = FALSE)  # random predictors
mc_ci <- function(p) {
  se <- sqrt(p * (1 - p) / reps)
  sprintf("%s (%s–%s)", pct(p), pct(max(0, p - 1.96 * se)), pct(min(1, p + 1.96 * se)))
}
```

# Executive summary

::: {.summary}
**Power check, Study 1.** The proposal says N = `r N_target` gives 80% power for small effects (f² = `r f2_main`). That's correct (`r pct(p_claim)`), but only for one predictor with complete, error-free data. If RQ1 tests the three stressors together, power is `r pct(p_block)` at N = `r N_target`; 80% needs `r n_block`. With realistic missing data and measurement error, power falls to `r pct(p_real)`. The minimum N of `r N_min` gives `r pct(p_min)`. Subgroup, moderation and country comparisons are underpowered, so they should be exploratory.

**Recommendations:** name one primary test per thesis, recruit at least `r N_gross` completed surveys to keep `r N_target` valid, justify f² from prior studies, keep K10 continuous and set a minimum sample per country.
:::

# Overview

**Question.** Does N = `r N_target` give 80% power to detect small adjusted effects (f² = `r f2_main`) in the Study 1 regression models?

**Method.** Analytic power from the noncentral F distribution (the G\*Power method), plus `r format(reps, big.mark = ",")` simulated datasets per scenario for risks a formula can't handle. Code: <https://github.com/delphinepadang/robust_future>

## Assumptions

```{r}
#| label: tbl-assumptions
#| tbl-cap: "Assumptions. All results below are computed from these values."
ktab(data.frame(
  Parameter = c("Valid sample size (target / minimum)", "Effect size", "Significance level",
                "Predictors in model (full / subgroup)", "Missing data (complete-case)",
                "Exclusions at data-quality screening", "Reliability (climate items / K10)",
                "Linkage consent (RQ4)", "RQ3 subgroup size", "Interaction effect",
                "Correlation among the three stressors", "Recontact opt-in / wave response"),
  Value = c(sprintf("%d / %d", N_target, N_min),
            sprintf("f² = %.2f (partial r = %s)", f2_main, sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.2f", f2_to_r(f2_main)))),
            sprintf("α = %.2f", alpha_main),
            sprintf("%d / %d", P, P_sub), pct(miss), pct(excl),
            sprintf("%.2f / %.2f", rel_x, rel_y), pct(consent), n_sub,
            sprintf("f² = %.2f", f2_int),
            sprintf("%s (.50 in risk scenario)", sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.2f", rho_main))),
            sprintf("%s / %s", pct(optin), pct(resp))),
  Source = c("Programme Proposal", "Programme Proposal", "Programme Proposal", "Assumed",
             "Assumed", "Assumed", "Assumed", "Assumed", "Project Plan (80–120)",
             "Assumed", "Assumed", "Project Plan")
), align = "llr")
```

## Main results

```{r}
#| label: tbl-key
#| tbl-cap: "Power for the target effect unless noted. 'Valid responses needed' adds back cases lost to missing data or non-consent."
rows <- list(
  list("Stated claim: 1 focal predictor",            N_target, f2_main, 1, P,     1, alpha_main),
  list("Stated minimum sample",                      N_min,    f2_main, 1, P,     1, alpha_main),
  list("RQ1: three stressors as one block (3 df)",   N_target, f2_main, 3, P,     1, alpha_main),
  list(sprintf("RQ1: each stressor, Bonferroni (α = %s/3)", a_lab), N_target, f2_main, 1, P, 1, alpha_main / 3),
  list("Missing data (complete-case)",               N_cc,     f2_main, 1, P,     1 - miss, alpha_main),
  list("Measurement error",                          N_target, f2_att,  1, P,     1, alpha_main),
  list("Missing data + measurement error",           N_cc,     f2_att,  1, P,     1 - miss, alpha_main),
  list("RQ4: linkage consent",                       N_link,   f2_main, 1, P,     consent, alpha_main),
  list("RQ3 subgroup (subgroup n)",                  n_sub,    f2_main, 1, P_sub, NA, alpha_main),
  list(sprintf("Interaction effect (f² = %.2f)", f2_int), N_target, f2_int, 1, P + 1, 1, alpha_main)
)
key <- do.call(rbind, lapply(rows, \(r) {
  n80 <- n_for_power(r[[3]], u = r[[4]], p = r[[5]], alpha = r[[7]])
  data.frame(Scenario = r[[1]], `Analysed N` = r[[2]],
             Power = pct(power_f2(r[[3]], r[[2]], u = r[[4]], p = r[[5]], alpha = r[[7]])),
             `Analysed N for 80%` = n80,
             `Valid responses needed` = if (is.na(r[[6]])) "—" else as.character(ceiling(n80 / r[[6]])),
             check.names = FALSE)
}))
ktab(key, align = "lrrrr")
```

::: {.callout-note}
G\*Power's method assumes fixed predictors. Survey predictors are measured, which gives slightly lower power (`r pct(p_strict)` instead of `r pct(p_claim)` for the stated claim). The conclusions are unchanged.
:::

## Additional risks

```{r}
#| label: tbl-risks
#| tbl-cap: "Power at the target sample size under each risk. (sim) = simulation; (approx.) = analytic approximation."
risks <- data.frame(
  Risk = c(
    "K10 dichotomised at 'high distress' (top 20%) (sim)",
    "Mild climate year: exposure SD 70% of usual (approx.)",
    "Countries unbalanced 75/25: country interaction (approx.)",
    "Stressors correlated (r = .5), f² from single-stressor studies",
    "10% careless responders not removed (sim)",
    "20% careless responders not removed (sim)",
    "True effect smaller than planned (f² = 0.015)",
    "Skewed K10 analysed with OLS (sim)",
    "20 covariate terms instead of 12"
  ),
  Power = pct(c(
    sim["top20"],
    power_f2(r_to_f2(restrict(f2_to_r(f2_main), 0.7)), N_target),
    power_f2(f2_int * (0.75 * 0.25) / 0.25, N_target, p = P + 1),
    power_f2(f2_main * (1 - r2_j(0.5)), N_target),
    sim["care10"], sim["care20"],
    power_f2(0.015, N_target),
    sim["skewed"],
    power_f2(f2_main, N_target, p = 20)
  )),
  `What to do` = c(
    "Keep K10 continuous; report cut-offs descriptively",
    "Check exposure spread at the mid-fieldwork review",
    "Set per-country minimums (e.g. 150 each)",
    "Base f² on partial effects; report VIFs",
    "Preregister screening rules",
    "Report results with and without exclusions",
    "Plan on a conservative f²",
    "Not a power risk; use robust SEs",
    "Minor"
  ),
  check.names = FALSE
)
ktab(risks, align = "lrl")
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## Don't look at outcomes during fieldwork
Checking results halfway (e.g. at the 4 June review) and again at the end raises false positives from `r pct(alpha_main)` to `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * two_looks)`. Monitor recruitment counts only.
:::

## Power curves

```{r}
#| label: fig-power
#| fig-cap: "Power to detect the target effect as sample size increases."
ns <- seq(150, 800, by = 5)
curves <- rbind(
  data.frame(N = ns, Test = "1 predictor",
             Power = sapply(ns, \(n) power_f2(f2_main, n))),
  data.frame(N = ns, Test = "3-predictor block",
             Power = sapply(ns, \(n) power_f2(f2_main, n, u = 3))),
  data.frame(N = ns, Test = "1 predictor, Bonferroni (α/3)",
             Power = sapply(ns, \(n) power_f2(f2_main, n, alpha = alpha_main / 3)))
)

ggplot(curves, aes(N, Power, colour = Test)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.80, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(N_min, N_target), linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
  annotate("text", x = c(N_min, N_target), y = 0.12,
           label = paste("N =", c(N_min, N_target)),
           hjust = -0.1, size = 3.2, colour = "grey40") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#4E9AC7", "#5DB88A", "#9C8FD0")) +
  labs(x = "Analysed sample size (N)", y = "Power", colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

# Evidence

## Sample size and effect size

```{r}
#| label: tbl-n
#| tbl-cap: "Power for the target effect by analysed sample size."
n_vals <- c(N_target, N_cc, 300, N_min)
ktab(data.frame(N = n_vals,
                 Power = pct(sapply(n_vals, \(n) power_f2(f2_main, n)))),
      align = "rr")
```

N for 80% power: **`r n_for_power(f2_main)`**; for 90% power: **`r n_for_power(f2_main, target = 0.90)`**.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sens
#| tbl-cap: "Power if the true effect differs from the target."
f2_vals <- c(0.010, 0.015, 0.020, 0.025, 0.030)
ktab(data.frame(
  `f²` = sprintf("%.3f", f2_vals),
  `Partial r` = sprintf("%.2f", f2_to_r(f2_vals)),
  `Power, N = 400` = pct(sapply(f2_vals, \(f) power_f2(f, N_target))),
  `Power, N = 340` = pct(sapply(f2_vals, \(f) power_f2(f, N_cc))),
  check.names = FALSE), align = "rrrr")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-detect
#| tbl-cap: "Smallest effect detectable with 80% power (one predictor)."
n_vals <- c(N_target, N_cc, N_link, N_min, 200)
sub_vals <- c(120, n_sub, 80, 60)
f2_full <- sapply(n_vals, \(n) f2_detectable(n))
f2_sub  <- sapply(sub_vals, \(n) f2_detectable(n, p = P_sub))
ktab(data.frame(
  Model = c(rep(sprintf("Full (%d predictors)", P), length(n_vals)),
            rep(sprintf("Subgroup (%d predictors)", P_sub), length(sub_vals))),
  n = c(n_vals, sub_vals),
  `f²` = sprintf("%.3f", c(f2_full, f2_sub)),
  `Partial r` = sprintf("%.2f", f2_to_r(c(f2_full, f2_sub))),
  check.names = FALSE), align = "lrrr")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-rq4-cluster
#| tbl-cap: "RQ4: area-level exposure. Design effect = 1 + (m − 1) × ICC, where ICC is the outcome's residual intra-area correlation."
clus <- data.frame(m = c(5, 10, 10, 25), icc = c(0.02, 0.02, 0.05, 0.05))
clus$deff  <- 1 + (clus$m - 1) * clus$icc
clus$n_eff <- N_target / clus$deff
ktab(data.frame(
  `People per area` = clus$m,
  ICC = clus$icc,
  `Design effect` = sprintf("%.2f", clus$deff),
  `Effective N` = round(clus$n_eff),
  Power = pct(sapply(clus$n_eff, \(n) power_f2(f2_main, n))),
  check.names = FALSE), align = "rrrrr")
```

## Measurement and design

```{r}
#| label: tbl-rel
#| tbl-cap: "Measurement error (approx.): observed r = true r × √(rel x × rel y)."
rel <- data.frame(rel_x = c(1, rel_x, 0.7, 0.6), rel_y = c(1, rel_y, rel_y, rel_y))
rel$f2_obs <- r_to_f2(f2_to_r(f2_main) * sqrt(rel$rel_x * rel$rel_y))
ktab(data.frame(
  `Climate items` = sprintf("%.2f", rel$rel_x),
  K10 = sprintf("%.2f", rel$rel_y),
  `Observed f²` = sprintf("%.4f", rel$f2_obs),
  `Power at N = 400` = pct(sapply(rel$f2_obs, \(f) power_f2(f, N_target))),
  `N for 80%` = sapply(rel$f2_obs, n_for_power),
  check.names = FALSE), align = "rrrrr")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-corr
#| tbl-cap: "Correlated stressors: unique effect if f² came from single-stressor studies."
rho <- c(0, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7)
ktab(data.frame(
  `Correlation among stressors` = sprintf("%.1f", rho),
  VIF = sprintf("%.2f", 1 / (1 - sapply(rho, r2_j))),
  `Partial f²` = sprintf("%.4f", f2_main * (1 - sapply(rho, r2_j))),
  `Power at N = 400` = pct(sapply(rho, \(r) power_f2(f2_main * (1 - r2_j(r)), N_target))),
  check.names = FALSE), align = "rrrr")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-range
#| tbl-cap: "Exposure range restriction (approx., Thorndike Case II): one fieldwork window may miss drought or flood."
k <- c(1, 0.8, 0.7, 0.5)
f2_k <- r_to_f2(restrict(f2_to_r(f2_main), k))
ktab(data.frame(
  `Exposure SD (vs usual)` = pct(k),
  `Observed f²` = sprintf("%.4f", f2_k),
  `Power at N = 400` = pct(sapply(f2_k, \(f) power_f2(f, N_target))),
  check.names = FALSE), align = "rrr")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-cov
#| tbl-cap: "Number of predictors in the model."
p_vals <- c(12, 16, 20, 25)
ktab(data.frame(
  `Predictors in model` = p_vals,
  `Power at N = 400` = pct(sapply(p_vals, \(p) power_f2(f2_main, N_target, p = p))),
  check.names = FALSE), align = "rr")
```

## Simulation

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sim
#| tbl-cap: "Rejection rates with 95% Monte Carlo intervals (target sample size, assumed stressor correlation, full covariate set)."
ktab(data.frame(
  Scenario = c("No true effect (Type I error check)", "Planned effect, normal errors",
               "Skewed outcome, OLS", "Outcome split at the median (logistic)",
               "Outcome split at top 20% (logistic)", "10% careless responders",
               "20% careless responders"),
  `Rejection rate` = unname(sapply(sim, mc_ci)),
  check.names = FALSE), align = "lr")
```

**Checks.** With no true effect the simulation rejects `r pct(sim["null"])` of the time (target `r pct(alpha_main)`). At the planned effect it gives `r pct(sim["baseline"])`, matching the random-predictor calculation (`r pct(p_strict)`); G\*Power's fixed-predictor method gives `r pct(p_claim)`.

## Recruitment and cohort

```{r}
#| label: tbl-recruit
#| tbl-cap: "Completed surveys needed, and the Project Plan's 280–460 range."
excls <- c(0.10, excl, 0.20, 0.30)
ktab(data.frame(
  `Exclusion rate` = pct(excls),
  `Completions for 400 valid` = ceiling(N_target / (1 - excls)),
  `Valid from 280` = floor(280 * (1 - excls)),
  `Valid from 460` = floor(460 * (1 - excls)),
  check.names = FALSE), align = "rrrr")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-cohort
#| tbl-cap: "Cohort size if retention applies only to those who opt in to recontact."
coh <- data.frame(optin = c(optin, 0.8), resp = c(resp, resp))
ktab(data.frame(
  `Recontact opt-in` = pct(coh$optin),
  `Wave response` = pct(coh$resp),
  `Wave 2 n` = round(N_target * coh$optin * coh$resp),
  `Wave 3 n` = round(N_target * coh$optin * coh$resp^2),
  check.names = FALSE), align = "rrrr")
```
